legend: It is almost Valentine's Day and Bob has found the perfect gift for Alice: a permutation of the integers 0,...,n−1$$$0, ..., n-1$$$! Bob knows that MEX is Alice's favorite function, and for this reason he wants to write for each index i$$$i$$$, the sum of MEX over all subarrays of the permutation that contain index i$$$i$$$. Unfortunately this is difficult for Bob to compute so he needs your help.

Formally, you are given a permutation a1,...,an$$$a_1, ..., a_n$$$ consisting of (distinct) integers 0,...,n−1$$$0, ..., n-1$$$. For each 1≤i≤n$$$1 \leq i \leq n$$$, determine the sum of MEX(a[l,r])$$$\text{MEX}(a[l, r])$$$ for each 1≤l≤r≤n$$$1 \leq l \leq r \leq n$$$ where a[l,r]$$$a[l, r]$$$ represents the subarray al,al+1,...ar$$$a_l, a_{l+1}, ... a_r$$$, and MEX(b)$$$\text{MEX}(b)$$$ outputs the smallest non-negative integer k$$$k$$$ such that k$$$k$$$ doesn't appear in b$$$b$$$.
input: The first line of input will contain a single integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤2⋅105$$$1 \leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — denoting the size of the permutation Bob found. The next line will contain n$$$n$$$ distinct integers a1,...,an$$$a_1, ..., a_n$$$ (0≤ai≤n−1$$$0 \leq a_i \leq n-1$$$) — describing the permutation itself.
output: The output will consist of n$$$n$$$ lines. On the i$$$i$$$th line, output the sum of MEX over all subarrays of a$$$a$$$ containing index i$$$i$$$.
